evidence: The knob really is gone, but the README diff hunk (F4) shows the PR itself deleting `--workers <N> (default 4)` from the documented usage, so the removal was deliberate and documented, not a silent side effect; the agent's claim that no in-repo caller passed it is unrefuted in the packet. freeze-suite.js's renderReport printed `Next: ... node eval/baseline.js --out-dir`, which is wrong when compare.js is the caller; 4359d50 replaced it with a line stating only what the command guarantees, avoiding the caller-flag the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: When a command gains a second caller, read its user-facing output for lines that assume the first caller's workflow and cut them to what the command itself guarantees.

evidence: The reviewer proposed both skipping the default-path join/split and banning commas; the agent banned commas but kept the round-trip citing [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow], and in d35f3e9 called that same round-trip 'serialization for its own sake' and removed it after it resurfaced as F8-F10. The comma ban was apt; the dataflow citation was pasted onto keeping an encode/decode loop.
guidance_note: When a value is encoded to a string only to be decoded in the same function, delete the round-trip rather than constraining the value so the round-trip is lossless.

evidence: a6397da made selection match on directory basename while compare.js passes manifest names as --cases, and the PR's own censusCases test 'the count keys off the manifest name, not the case directory name' treated divergence as supported, so a renamed dir would now fail the gate. d35f3e9 makes parseCaseManifest refuse name != basename and rewrites that test.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the 240-minute timeout and its headroom math are in the original eval.yml change (the hunk), and a6397da did not touch eval.yml. The derivation ignored freeze-suite.js's 120-minute per-replay deadline; d35f3e9 re-derived 6x27+120 and set 300.
guidance_note: When deriving a CI timeout from a scheduler's behavior, enumerate the scheduler's own failure paths (deadline kills, dead lanes, requeues) and size for the worst one you claim to cover.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the stale 'same env var the action uses' paragraph and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=…` synopsis are original text made stale by the PR's own eval.yml switch to lane secrets; a6397da only edited the --credentials entry above them. d35f3e9 rewrote both to describe the default and --credentials paths.

evidence: d35f3e9 (F12 fix) re-derived 300 min from 'a lane carries at most 7' plus one stall but did not account for a dead lane redistributing jobs (~9 per survivor, 8x27+120≈336). The packet does not show runLane, but the agent confirmed the shared-queue requeue behavior and 80a29bd raised the ceiling to 350 with that derivation.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 1e765d3 touched only README and a test, and --credentials with --reuse-candidate was ignored since the original PR; the round-3 summary had already raised this as an out-of-diff S2 at compare.js:513 and it went unaddressed until round 4. The agent refused the combination, matching --out + --reuse-candidate, instead of printing a notice.
guidance_note: When adding a flag to a command with mutually exclusive modes, decide its status in every mode (used, refused) in the same commit as the flag.

narrative: The PR switched compare.js to replay through freeze-suite.js. The costliest chain started at F3, where the agent banned commas in names but kept the default-path join/split; then a6397da (the F6 fix) moved selection onto unvalidated directory basenames, which reopened the comma hole and split case identity in two (F8-F11, four threads on one defect). Doc staleness from the runner and credential switch came back one copy at a time (F4→F7, F14→F15), and the CI timeout bound was re-derived twice (F12→F17). Round 4 was avoidable: F17 was the remainder of F12's fix, and F18 repeated a round-3 out-of-diff finding the agent never acted on; the PR then hit the 5-round cap and the last delta was reviewed locally.
guidance_observations: Out-of-diff findings in a round summary (round 3's --credentials/--reuse-candidate S2) need a reply and a fix like inline threads, or they come back as a new round.

Several flagged findings were original-PR defects anchored on a fix commit; a pre-push sweep of the original diff's docs and help text for old env-var names and process names would have caught F5, F14 and F15 before review.

The agent's eventual fixes (one case identity, refusing a contradictory flag, a CLI-spawning test) were structurally better than the reviewer's suggestions, but each came one round late because the first fix addressed only the instance named.
